::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 18th 1874  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Bodleian Library, Oxford: Bryce 156 (microfilm) ff21-2
:::

My dear [Miss Freeman](people/person_524.qmd)
Many thanks for the extract. I am very glad the answer has come to be gibbetted! People ought to have the penalty of exposing themselves so wonderfully.

You and Moneyspinner ([Miss Marriott](people/person_958.qmd) of Hythe) are the most effective [Spiders](organizations/other_116.qmd).[^1]

I have taken her sum, because she did it in a conversation, but your nines, for nobody else attempted them[^2]

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Freeman had taken part in the Spider Society essay competitions in *MP*.
[^2]: This confirms the identification of Freeman as 'Pisa', for *MP* (July 1874) 8, prints 'Money Spinner''s 'Multiplying 4265 by 3902' and comments 'PISA is the only one who has \\"cast out the nines\\"'.
